```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## R Markdown intro
R Markdown is a powerful format that combines narrative text, executable R code, and the resulting output into a single document. This integration promotes reproducible research by enabling others to see both the code and its outputs alongside the explanations, making it easier to verify and update analyses seamlessly.


This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
library(ggplot2)
data(mtcars)

```

## Simple analysis and plot

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
summary(mtcars$mpg)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=mpg)) + geom_histogram(binwidth=5)

```
EX:The product of two numbers $3 \times 4 = 12$ demonstrates simple multiplication inline. Similarly, $7 \times 8 = 56$ shows another example.

```{Equation display}
Here is a displayed multiplication equation:

$$
3 \times 4 = 12
$$

And another one:

$$
7 \times 8 = 56
$$

```

Comparing the .Rmd source and its HTML rendering revealed how markdown text, La-TeX math expressions, and R code chunks are cleanly transformed into formatted, displayed equations, and interactive plots without extra manual formatting. One formatting surprise during knitting was the smooth handling of La-TeX formulas with minimal syntax, making math expressions highly readable in the output. Additionally, automatic code execution and output embedding eliminate redundancy and future-proofs analyses against manual errors. Overall, this workflow provides a well-organized, reproducible, and elegant reporting experience that I would prefer over separate script and narrative files.


Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
